body.statement: For every sequence in \(\mathcal P_n\), including sequences with \(H\to\infty\), \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{bc}}-\tau=-L+o_{\mathbb P}(s)\), \(\widehat V/s^2\to_{\mathbb P}1\), and the primitive conditional block-dependence and score-diffuseness conditions yield \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}|\mathbb P_P\{(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{bc}}-\tau)/\sqrt{\widehat V}\le z\mid M,\Omega\}-\Phi(z)|\to0\). Consequently, \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n}\mathbb P_P\{\tau\in\mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha}\mid M,\Omega\}\to1-\alpha\). This strictly extends Choi and Yuan (2024), Theorem 3.1, for the same native subgroup estimator from \(q=0,H=1\) to fixed \(q\ge1\), growing \(H\), and a feasible nonzero curvature correction.
body.justification: The derived dependency-graph limit and feasible studentization convert weak-signal deterministic-MNAR completion into implementable inference for a sustained causal effect.
body.gap: Choi and Yuan cover a one-date independent-noise subgroup average; Cen and Lam cover residual HAC for loading scores; Su, Wang, and Wang cover regression coefficients from alternating maximization.
body.consumer: The confidence interval directly supports a reanalysis of the SEC Tick Size Pilot's average sustained liquidity effect over the realized treated cohort and post window.

obligation.what_is_open: Establish the native expansion, feasible curvature rate, residual covariance rate, and relative fitted-weight consistency required before the proved oracle score limit can be studentized.
obligation.obstruction: The causal cancellation, banded-Toeplitz variance comparison, conditional Gaussian score limit, and coverage reduction are closed, but each remaining stochastic error is a conclusion of the unresolved native-transfer theorem. Using those conclusions now would make this theorem depend on an unproved target rather than on the frozen primitives.
obligation.attempted: The exact causal error identity was combined with the native theorem's proposed decomposition. Variance consistency was reduced by an explicit quadratic-form expansion to covariance consistency and relative fitted-weight consistency. The conditional score central limit theorem was proved directly from the cited finite-range normal bound.
obligation.partial_result:
The causal reduction is exact.  On \(G\times W\), \(\mathrm{ass:common\mbox{-}start\mbox{-}mask}\) gives \(A_{it}=1\), and \(\mathrm{ass:causal\mbox{-}consistency}\) therefore gives \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{it}=Y_{it}(1)\).  Comparing the definitions of \(\widehat\tau\) and \(\tau\) yields
\[
 \widehat\tau-\tau
 =-\frac1{gH}\sum_{i\in G,t\in W}(\widehat M_{it}-M_{it}).
\]
Consequently, if \(\mathrm{thm:native\mbox{-}second\mbox{-}order\mbox{-}transfer}\) were established, its decomposition and \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{bc}}=\widehat\tau+\widehat B_2\) would give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \widehat\tau_{\mathrm{bc}}-\tau
 &=-L-Q-R_{\mathrm{agg}}+\widehat B_2\\
 &=-L-(Q-B_2)-R_{\mathrm{agg}}+(\widehat B_2-B_2)\\
 &=-L+o_{\mathbb P}(s),
\end{aligned}
\]
where the final equality follows from the standard-error calculations recorded for the native-transfer target.

For the studentization reduction, let \(d=\widehat w-w\), and let \(\Gamma_q\) and \(\widehat\Gamma_q\) be the \(T\times T\) banded Toeplitz matrices whose \((u,v)\) entries are \(1\{|u-v|\le q\}\gamma(v-u)\) and \(1\{|u-v|\le q\}\widehat\gamma(v-u)\), respectively.  By the definitions of \(s^2\) and \(\widehat V\),
\[
 s^2=\sum_{j=1}^N w_{j\cdot}^{\top}\Gamma_qw_{j\cdot},
 \qquad
 \widehat V=\sum_{j=1}^N(w_{j\cdot}+d_{j\cdot})^{\top}
 \widehat\Gamma_q(w_{j\cdot}+d_{j\cdot}).
\]
Fixed \(q\), the conditional moment bound, and \(\Delta_\gamma=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\) imply
\[
 \|\widehat\Gamma_q\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O_{\mathbb P}(1),
 \qquad
 \|\widehat\Gamma_q-\Gamma_q\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le(2q+1)\Delta_\gamma=o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\]
Expanding the two quadratic forms and applying Cauchy--Schwarz therefore gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 |\widehat V-s^2|
 &\le \|\widehat\Gamma_q\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \left(2\|w\|_F\|d\|_F+\|d\|_F^2\right)
 +\|\widehat\Gamma_q-\Gamma_q\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|w\|_F^2\\
 &=O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(
 \|w\|_F\|d\|_F+\|d\|_F^2+\Delta_\gamma\|w\|_F^2
 \right).
\end{aligned}
\]
The established score-diffuseness result gives \(\|w\|_F^2=O(s^2)\).  Hence the native-transfer conclusions \(\|d\|_F^2=o_{\mathbb P}(s^2)\) and \(\Delta_\gamma=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\) would imply
\[
 \frac{|\widehat V-s^2|}{s^2}
 =O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(
 \frac{\|w\|_F}{s}\frac{\|d\|_F}{s}
 +\frac{\|d\|_F^2}{s^2}+\Delta_\gamma\frac{\|w\|_F^2}{s^2}
 \right)=o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\]
The conditional score central limit theorem is proved in this dispatch.  Once the unresolved native-transfer inputs are available, conditional Slutsky applied to the last two displays yields the claimed studentized normal limit.  Since \(z_{1-\alpha/2}\) is finite for fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), evaluation at its two continuity points gives conditional coverage tending uniformly to \(1-\alpha\).  Thus the causal identity, variance comparison, score limit, and final coverage implication are closed; the only missing premise is the estimator-specific native second-order transfer and its plug-in conclusions.
